thread:
maria-finance: FYI — we received the renewal invoice for ACME Corp's private deployment (invoice 2024-ACME-4432) but the platform fee looks off. The invoice shows a full month of platform fee even though their renewal/proration should have started mid-cycle. Can someone confirm how we calculated the platform fee and whether a true-up is needed?

anna-accounting: Which line are you seeing that on? I pulled the PDF and I see both 'Platform License (annual)' and 'Support (tier 2) — monthly'.

maria-finance: Here's the relevant section from the invoice PDF I downloaded:```
1x Private Platform (annual) — $80,000.00
Prorated platform (Mar 15 - Mar 31) — $0.00 (line 7)
Support: Tier 2 monthly — $8,500.00
Total due: $88,500.00
```
It looks like the prorated platform line is zeroed out which seems wrong. They signed the private deploy contract 2024-03-15 and the billing period is monthly-to-annual conversion effective that date.

josh-sales: @maria-finance tagging — sales agreed on a mid-month pro-rate on the platform fee in the SOW. PO #98765 was created referencing the annual platform license prorated from 3/15. We should not charge a full year's platform on the first invoice.

anna-accounting: Hmm, our billing engine applies the annual platform fee immediately unless the contract flag 'deferred_proration' is set. Looks like that flag wasn't set on ACME. I'll pull the billing job logs.

billing-bot: Billing job 2024-03-16T04:12:08Z processed invoice 2024-ACME-4432. Applied product_id=private_platform_annual quantity=1 price=80000 prorate_flag=false

maria-finance: Great — thanks @billing-bot. So it's a config miss. Can we issue a credit or a corrected invoice and process a true-up for the prorated amount? Customer is already pushing for payment and their AP wants net-30.

anna-accounting: We can do a corrected invoice (credit mem + new invoice). For the true-up amount: prorated platform from 3/15–3/31 is 17/365 * $80,000 = ~$3,726. Do we want to credit the full annual and create a prorated invoice, or apply a credit memo for the difference?

lisa-legal: From a contract standpoint we should avoid issuing a brand-new annual invoice that contradicts the SOW. Credit memo + corrected invoice that matches the SOW is cleaner. Also need an approval from Sales leadership for the manual adjustment (audit trail).

josh-sales: I can provide written approval. I'll post the signed SOW excerpt to this thread and confirm with Acme that a corrected invoice is acceptable.

ben-customer-success: Heads-up — ACME's billing contact is Jane Park (jane.park@acme.com). She pinged support saying 'invoice doesn't match our PO', so this will help. I'll loop her in once we have the corrected doc.

anna-accounting: Plan: 1) Create credit memo for $80,000 2) Issue prorated invoice for $3,726 + support for remainder of month 3) Attach note referencing PO #98765 and SOW 4) Move payment terms to Net-30 and send to AP. Need approvals: @josh-sales (sales sign-off) and @maria-finance (finance) to authorize credit.

maria-finance: Approve. Please add a billing remark 'manual true-up per SOW, sales-approved'.

josh-sales: Approve. I'll attach the SOW excerpt and confirm with Jane.

anna-accounting: Doing the adjustments now. I'll upload the corrected invoice and credit memo to Stripe (invoice 2024-ACME-4432-REV1) and send to Jane. ETA 2 hours.

billing-bot: Action logged: created credit_memo=CM-4432-1, adjusted_invoice=INV-4432-R1, accounting_note='manual true-up per SOW'.

maria-finance: Thanks. One follow-up for close: we should update the onboarding checklist so 'deferred_proration' is validated on contract ingestion to prevent this. Can someone add a ticket?

josh-sales: I'll add a ticket in GH: redwood/sales-onboarding#204 and assign to @anna-accounting and @maria-finance.

ben-customer-success: I'll message Jane and confirm once she receives the corrected documents. :thumbsup:

lisa-legal: Also recommending we snapshot the SOW and attach to the invoice metadata for auditability. I'll coordinate with Contracts to add that step to the renewal playbook.

maria-finance: Perfect. Thanks everyone — closing the loop here once invoice is confirmed received by ACME.
